blogs.title: Beyond the Nausea: GLP-1 Agonists and a Rare Muscle Mystery
blogs.description: With the exponential rise in the use of semaglutide and tirzepatide for obesity and diabetes, clinicians must expand their toolkit of known adverse effects. This post discusses the emerging signal of muscle loss and rare immune-mediated reactions associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists, emphasizing the need for heightened pharmacovigilance in the era of 'weight-loss wonder drugs'.

blogs.title: Rhabdo or IMNM? When Muscle Injury Doesn't Just 'Go Away'
blogs.description: Not all drug-induced muscle breakdown is created equal. This post explores the critical clinical distinction between acute toxic rhabdomyolysis—which typically resolves with drug cessation and hydration—and Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy (IMNM), which presents with a progressive course and requires aggressive immunosuppression for recovery.

blogs.title: The Seronegative Trap: Diagnosing IMNM Without the Antibodies
blogs.description: What do you do when the myositis panel comes back negative? This post analyzes the diagnostic challenge of seronegative IMNM, discussing why the absence of HMGCR or SRP antibodies should not rule out the diagnosis and reinforcing the gold-standard role of muscle biopsy in confirming necrotizing myofibers and inflammatory infiltrates.

blogs.title: More Than Just Weak Legs: The Danger of Bulbar Involvement in Myopathy
blogs.description: Proximal muscle weakness is the classic presentation of myopathy, but it's the bulbar symptoms that kill. This post highlights the clinical significance of dysphagia and dysphonia in the context of IMNM, discussing the risks of aspiration and the necessity of early airway and swallow assessments in patients with progressive muscle decline.

blogs.title: The Delayed Fuse: Rethinking Temporal Relationships in Drug Reactions
blogs.description: We are taught that drug reactions happen quickly, but some triggers have a 'delayed fuse.' This post discusses the case of a single dose of semaglutide leading to peak muscle weakness four months later, challenging clinicians to consider distant triggers when evaluating autoimmune presentations and analyzing the WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre causality criteria.
